Team Astro Pebbles 

We’re a skilled team in coding, engineering and innovation, focused on solving space challenges. We’re undergraduates who are passionate about space driven by curiosity and the excitement of turning big ideas into real solutions.
summary:
Future Moon bases and Mars missions need places on Earth where teams can test rovers, ice drilling tools and habitats. Analog sites already exist in the Atacama Desert, Devon Island and Hawaii, but their data is scattered across many catalogs, missions and agencies, and many sites are not well characterized.
TerraTwin is a free web platform with three 3D globes for Earth, Mars and the Moon, using live NASA data along with radar and elevation data from ESA, JAXA and CSA. Users compare any Earth site with its Moon or Mars twin using a swipe slider. A planetary fingerprint shows where the two sites match and where they do not. Every site is labeled well studied, partly characterized or new candidate. A Mission Planner ranks sites for goals like ice drilling or rover mobility. A guided story tour links Shackleton Rim and Jezero to their Earth twins, and a literature back test checks the scoring against published field campaigns.
Anyone can nominate a new site, and an administrator checks the data before it goes live. TerraTwin serves mission planners, researchers, data analysts, universities, students and enthusiasts. Analogs cannot reproduce gravity, radiation and vacuum.
details:
The problem

Field rehearsals only give useful results when the test site matches the challenge being studied. The lunar south pole has steep crater rims, long shadows and frozen volatiles. Mars has ancient clay lakebeds and hyper-arid soils with oxidizing perchlorates and fine dust. No single place on Earth can copy all of these conditions at once. Mission planners therefore have to compare one environmental variable at a time. Today this means stitching together orbital data, published benchmarks and weather records from different agencies by hand.

What TerraTwin does

Three planetary globes. TerraTwin is built on CesiumJS and gives Earth, Mars and the Moon their own 3D globes. The Moon globe uses NASA Moon Trek LRO WAC global mosaics at 303 pixels per degree and LOLA elevation relief. The Mars globe uses NASA Mars Trek Viking MDIM21 color mosaics at 232 m and MGS MOLA elevation. The Earth globe shows a global satellite basemap with switchable NASA GIBS daily true color and land surface temperature layers.

Interactive split slider. Users compare an Earth analog with its off-world target side by side across four layers. These layers, satellite imagery, topographic slope, temperature swings and radar roughness. The radar layer draws on ESA Sentinel-1, JAXA PALSAR-2 and CSA RADARSAT.

Planetary fingerprint. A normalized radar chart shows how closely two sites match on slope and relief, temperature range, soil composition, ground ice, water traps and radar texture. Users can tune the weights against expert baseline presets to model their own mission tolerances. Every site is also labeled as well studied, partly characterized or new candidate.

Mission Planner. The planner lets users choose an engineering goal such as ice drilling and volatiles, rover mobility, subsurface lava tube habitat or thermal survival. The engine then recommends the top ranked Earth test sites. It always shows a physical limitations notice that explains what cannot be simulated.

Guided astronaut story tour. A step by step tour flies the camera from the Artemis targets of Shackleton Rim and Connecting Ridge to the Mars targets of Jezero and Gale Craters. It then moves to their Earth twins. Devon Island and Haughton Crater represent polar permafrost. Hawaii and Mount Teide represent basaltic lava tubes. The Atacama Desert represents hyper-arid chemistry.

Literature back test. A validation panel checks our scoring model against published field campaigns. These include the NASA Haughton-Mars Project, the NASA Astrobiology Institute, ESA PANGAEA and HI-SEAS. The panel shows whether the known benchmark sites rank near the top of the analog index. Anyone can open it to see the evidence behind the scores.

Open to anyone interested. TerraTwin is not limited to one group. Researchers, university teams, data analysts and mission planners, students and teachers and space enthusiasts can all explore real space agency data. They can check the values behind each site. They can also learn from the literature back test how scientists judge whether an Earth site is a good analog.

Community nominations with admin review. Anyone can propose a new analog with coordinates, terrain category, target body and photos. Each submission is stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with PostGIS and waits in a moderation queue. An administrator then checks whether the data is correct. Only an approved site appears on the globe. This review step follows the community nomination step.

Why it matters

For mission planners and scientists. TerraTwin brings planetary GIS, orbital radar and meteorological data into one screening tool. Teams can compare candidate field sites and check their operational limits before they pay for an expedition.

For researchers, universities, analysts and anyone interested in space. The platform needs only a modern web browser. There is no login, no special software and no paywall. Researchers and data analysts can screen candidate sites and inspect the data behind each score. University groups, students, teachers and enthusiasts can explore real space agency data. They can also learn why geological formations in their own region including Sri Lanka may have analog value.

Data and tools we used

CesiumJS. This is an open source WebGL globe engine under the Apache 2.0 license. It handles orbital tiles, atmosphere rendering and camera paths.

Supabase. This is a spatial database built on PostgreSQL 16 and PostGIS 3.4. It stores the locations and a telemetry cache and uses GiST spatial indexing and row level security and safe spatial queries.

NASA POWER. This service from LaRC uses MERRA-2 data to give surface climatology for the analog sites. It covers annual mean temperature and day and night swings and solar irradiance and humidity.

NASA GIBS and Earthdata. These EOSDIS services provide cached tile layers for MODIS Terra true color and land surface temperature.

NASA Solar System Treks. Moon Trek and Mars Trek with USGS Astrogeology provide LRO WAC mosaics and LOLA shaded relief and Viking MDIM21 color mosaics and MGS MOLA elevation.

NASA PDS Geosciences Orbital Data Explorer. The ODE REST service provides spectrometer and radiometer observations from MRO CRISM and SHARAD and LRO Diviner. Nodata values are masked.

NASA Image and Video Library. This library provides public domain rover and mission surface photos for the target reference cards.

ESA Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem. It provides Sentinel-1 radar surface roughness and Sentinel-2 mineral reflectance. This work contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data.

JAXA EORC. It provides the AW3D30 30 m digital surface model and ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L-band radar through G-Portal.

Canadian Space Agency Open Data. It provides RADARSAT-1 and RADARSAT Constellation Mission radar products under the Open Government Licence Canada.

Esri World Imagery. It provides the satellite basemap tiles for the Earth globe.

Wikimedia Commons. It provides open licensed photographs of Earth analog sites and they are credited on our Credits page.

What makes it creative

Instead of showing separate flat maps TerraTwin keeps three worlds in one interface. The swipe slider is a simple visual bridge between a Martian or lunar landscape and its Earth equivalent. The fingerprint turns many variables into one shape that anyone can read. The Mission Planner and the back test connect the tool to published aerospace research. The story tour and the back test panel make the same data useful for teaching and research.

What we considered and what it cannot do

No site on Earth can simulate everything. We state these limits inside the tool as well.

Gravity. Earth is 1.0 g or 9.81 m/s2. The Moon is about 0.17 g or 1.62 m/s2 and Mars is 0.38 g or 3.72 m/s2. Rover traction and wheel sinkage and soil bearing strength and spacesuit movement all change with gravity.

Radiation. Earth's magnetic field and thick atmosphere shield the ground from galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events. Surface radiation on the Moon and Mars is on the order of hundreds of mSv per year. Earth's average background is about 2.4 mSv per year.

Atmosphere and vacuum. Earth's sea level pressure is about 1013 mbar. Mars has a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere of about 6 mbar and the lunar surface is a near perfect vacuum. Sublimation, outgassing and heat loss behave very differently in these conditions.

Data calibration. NASA POWER gives real reference values but our similarity scores are normalized estimates for early screening of sites. They are not flight qualification.

Use of AI

We used generative AI tools in 2 ways. Claude from Anthropic helped write contents. Antigravity from Google helped with code scaffolding, PostGIS migration scripts and schema validation.
